title: Use plain channel send or receive instead of single-case select.
summary: Select statements with a single case can be replaced with a simple send or receive. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace for loop with call to copy.
summary: Use copy() for copying elements from one slice to another. For arrays of identical size, you can use simple assignment. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit comparison with boolean constant.
summary: A boolean expression can be used directly instead of comparing it with true or false. Use the expression itself, or its negation with !, to express the same condition without the redundant comparison. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace call to strings.Index with strings.Contains.
summary: When only checking whether a string or byte slice contains a value, use Contains instead of comparing the result of Index with zero or -1. This expresses the intent directly, without an explicit comparison of positions. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace call to bytes.Compare with bytes.Equal.
summary: When comparing byte slices for equality, use bytes.Equal instead of comparing the result of bytes.Compare with zero. bytes.Equal makes the intent clear, while bytes.Compare is useful when the ordering of the slices matters. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Drop unnecessary use of the blank identifier.
summary: In many cases, assigning to the blank identifier is unnecessary. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use for { ... } for infinite loops.
summary: For infinite loops, using for { ... } is the most idiomatic choice. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Simplify regular expression by using raw string literal.
summary: Raw string literals use backticks instead of quotation marks and do not support any escape sequences. This means that the backslash can be used freely, without the need of escaping. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Simplify returning boolean expression.
summary: An if statement that returns true when a condition holds, followed by a return of false, can be replaced with a single return of the condition. If the return values are reversed, return the negated condition instead. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit redundant nil check on slices, maps, and channels.
summary: The len function is defined for all slices, maps, and channels, even nil ones, which have a length of zero. It is not necessary to check for nil before checking that their length is not zero. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit default slice index.
summary: When slicing, the second index defaults to the length of the value, making s[n:len(s)] and s[n:] equivalent. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use a single append to concatenate two slices.
summary: When two slices have the same type, a loop that only appends elements from one to the other can be replaced with a single call to append. Use append(x, y...) to append all elements of y to x, making the concatenation explicit without a loop. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace time.Now().Sub(x) with time.Since(x).
summary: The time.Since helper has the same effect as using time.Now().Sub(x) but is easier to read. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use a type conversion instead of manually copying struct fields.
summary: Two struct types with identical fields can be converted between each other. In older versions of Go, the fields had to have identical struct tags. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace manual trimming with strings.TrimPrefix.
summary: Instead of using strings.HasPrefix and manual slicing, use the strings.TrimPrefix function. If the string doesn’t start with the prefix, the original string will be returned. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use copy for sliding elements.
summary: copy() permits using the same source and destination slice, even with overlapping ranges. This makes it ideal for sliding elements in a slice. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Simplify make call by omitting redundant arguments.
summary: The make function has default values for the length and capacity arguments. For channels, the length defaults to zero, and for slices, the capacity defaults to the length. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit redundant nil check in type assertion.
summary: A successful type assertion implies that the original interface value is not nil. When checking the boolean result of a type assertion, an additional nil check on that interface is redundant. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Merge variable declaration and assignment.
summary: A variable declaration immediately followed by its initial assignment can be combined into a declaration with an initializer, as long as the initializer does not refer to the variable itself. This keeps the variable and its initial value together while preserving any explicit type needed for the declaration. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit redundant control flow.
summary: Functions that have no return value do not need a return statement as the final statement of the function. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Replace x.Sub(time.Now()) with time.Until(x).
summary: The time.Until helper has the same effect as using x.Sub(time.Now()) but is easier to read. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Don’t use fmt.Sprintf("%s", x) unnecessarily.
summary: In many instances, there are easier and more efficient ways of getting a value’s string representation. Whenever a value’s underlying type is a string already, or the type has a String method, they should be used directly. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Simplify error construction with fmt.Errorf.
summary: The fmt.Errorf function formats a message and returns it as an error. Use it instead of wrapping a call to fmt.Sprintf in errors.New to construct an error with a formatted message in a single call. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Range over the string directly.
summary: Ranging over a string will yield byte offsets and runes. If the offset isn’t used, this is functionally equivalent to converting the string to a slice of runes and ranging over that. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use bytes.Buffer.String or bytes.Buffer.Bytes.
summary: bytes.Buffer has both a String and a Bytes method. It is almost never necessary to use string(buf.Bytes()) or []byte(buf.String()) – simply use the other method. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Omit redundant nil check around loop.
summary: You can use range on nil slices and maps, the loop will simply never execute. This makes an additional nil check around the loop unnecessary. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use sort.Ints(x), sort.Float64s(x), and sort.Strings(x).
summary: The sort.Ints, sort.Float64s and sort.Strings functions are easier to read than sort.Sort(sort.IntSlice(x)), sort.Sort(sort.Float64Slice(x)) and sort.Sort(sort.StringSlice(x)). It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Unnecessary guard around call to delete.
summary: Calling delete on a nil map is a no-op. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Use result of type assertion to simplify cases.
summary: A type switch can bind the matched value to a variable using switch v := x.(type). Within a case that lists a single type, the variable has that type. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Redundant call to net/http.CanonicalHeaderKey in method call on net/http.Header.
summary: The methods on net/http.Header, namely Add, Del, Get and Set, already canonicalize the given header name. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Unnecessary guard around map access.
summary: When accessing a map key that doesn’t exist yet, one receives a zero value. Often, the zero value is a suitable value, for example when using append or doing integer math. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Elaborate way of sleeping.
summary: Using a select statement with a single case receiving from the result of time.After is a very elaborate way of sleeping that can much simpler be expressed with a simple call to time.Sleep. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Unnecessarily complex way of printing formatted string.
summary: Instead of using fmt.Print(fmt.Sprintf(...)), one can use fmt.Printf(...). It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Unnecessary use of fmt.Sprint.
summary: Calling fmt.Sprint with a single string argument is unnecessary and identical to using the string directly. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the simple group of checks.

title: Type assertion to current type.
summary: The type assertion x.(SomeInterface), when x already has type SomeInterface, can only fail if x is nil. Usually, this is left-over code from when x had a different type and you can safely delete the type assertion. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the simple group of checks.
